candidates.title: Four production #[allow(clippy::...)] sites in the 5a manifest carry no written rationale, so the census's sanctioned-by-construction claim is false at those four

evidence.command: git grep -c -E '^[[:space:]]*#!?\[allow\(' 077dbe2c -- <the 28 manifest paths> ; then for each hit: git show 077dbe2c:<file> | sed -n '<site-1>,<site+12>p'
evidence.output: Census over the 5a manifest: 18 of 28 files, 71 attribute-position openers, split 43 test-side / 28 production-side. Of the 28 production sites, 24 carry an inline bound and 4 carry none: policy/orchestration.rs:230 '#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)]' directly above 'pub fn write_checkpoint'; setup/node_graph.rs:297 '#[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss)]' above 'fn new' in 'impl NodeOpenings' (computes 'q: 1.0 / (len as f64)'); setup/node_graph.rs:488 '#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_wrap, clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]' inside 'build_chain_node_graph' over '(0..n_stages as i32).map(NodeId)'; stochastic/noise_key.rs:245 '#[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss)]' above 'fn chain_position_key(n_o: usize, pos: usize) -> f64 { (n_o - pos) as f64 }'. Contrast setup/stochastic_pipeline.rs:160, whose allow is followed by '// block_idx is a small count (< 1000 in practice); fits in i32.', and setup/orchestration.rs, whose train_inner allow carries an explicit '// Rationale:' line. A fifth site, setup/node_graph.rs:905 above 'pool_cut_stride', has a long formula doc but no lint-specific bound; it is cited, not anchored, as the borderline case. An earlier count of 73 openers was an over-count: 'git grep -c -E "#!?\[allow\("' also matches the phrase '#[allow(dead_code)] refires once ...' written inside comments at setup/mod.rs:312 and setup/bucket_topology.rs:26, so the count must anchor the attribute to line start.
evidence.reading: The prior register excludes the allow census by construction on the ground that every site is sanctioned. That holds for 24 of 28 production sites and fails at four. An allow with no stated bound is an unbounded suppression: a later edit that widens the value range keeps compiling with no signal. chain_position_key is the sharpest of the four because the cast feeds a deterministic noise-ordering key, so the safe-range claim is a determinism surface and nothing on the page states it.

candidates.fixShape: Add one clause to each of the four sites naming the range that makes the cast safe (opening count, stage count, chain position, checkpoint iteration), in the same '// Rationale:' form the 24 sibling sites already use, or narrow the cast so no allow is needed at all. Prefer narrowing at chain_position_key, where the bound is the claim a determinism reader needs. This is comment-only or cast-shape-only, so no numeric result moves; bound it with the parity goldens in crates/cobre-sddp/tests/parity.rs and crates/cobre-sddp/tests/common/parity_hash.rs plus the rank-invariance harness in crates/cobre-sddp/tests/common/permute.rs.

candidates.title: ncs_stochastic_dormant_for_test ships in the default public API while its four sibling test hooks in the same file are test-support-gated

evidence.command: git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/setup/accessors.rs (read in full, 370 lines) ; git grep -n -w ncs_stochastic_dormant_for_test 077dbe2c -- crates ; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/Cargo.toml
evidence.output: In accessors.rs, 'set_risk_measures', 'set_scheduler', 'set_hardest_first_claim_order' and 'training_ctx' each sit under '#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]'. 'ncs_stochastic_dormant_for_test' is declared plain: '#[must_use] pub fn ncs_stochastic_dormant_for_test(&self) -> Vec<Vec<bool>>', documented as 'reconstructed for the out-of-crate tests/ harness'. Its only caller anywhere in the workspace at the pin is crates/cobre-sddp/tests/deterministic.rs:2014, inside the D18 per-stage NCS commissioning dormancy test whose doc block runs :1971-1980; that test is not feature-gated. Cargo.toml declares 'default = ["highs"]' and 'test-support = ["cobre-core/test-support"]', so test-support is off by default.
evidence.reading: The method allocates a Vec<Vec<bool>> reconstruction of dormancy state that no production path reads, and its own name carries the _for_test suffix, so it is a test seam published to every downstream consumer of the crate. The same file already applies the correct gate four times, which is what makes this a miss rather than a design choice: the pattern exists and one member of the family does not follow it.

candidates.fixShape: Either move the method under the same '#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]' as its four siblings and declare test-support as a required feature of the one consuming test, or, if the published surface is intended, drop the _for_test suffix and document it as a supported query. Prefer the gate. Note the real trade-off the gate carries: the D18 dormancy test runs today under a plain 'cargo test --workspace', so gating it moves that coverage behind a feature flag and the station should say so rather than let it silently drop. No production caller exists either way, so the solve paths are untouched; parity goldens and the rank-invariance harness bound the change.

candidates.title: train_inner hand-mirrors the 19-field TrainingContext and the StageContext literal that accessors.rs already constructs, and the training_ctx constructor it duplicates is cfg-gated with no production consumer

evidence.command: git grep -n -w 'training_ctx' 077dbe2c -- crates ; git grep -n -w 'stage_ctx' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/src crates/cobre-cli crates/cobre-python ; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/setup/accessors.rs | sed -n '262,300p' ; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/setup/orchestration.rs | sed -n '168,215p'
evidence.output: accessors.rs:274 declares '#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))] #[must_use] pub fn training_ctx(&self) -> TrainingContext<'_>' and builds a 19-field literal. orchestration.rs:177, inside train_inner, builds the same 19 fields in the same order from the same expressions, down to the identical tail 'dcs: self.cut_management.cut_selection.as_ref().and_then(DcsParams::from_strategy)' and the same 'let tr = &self.scenario_libraries.training;' preamble. The only training_ctx() call sites in cobre-sddp are setup/tests.rs:862, :6460 and :6516; there is no production caller. The sibling path does the opposite: at orchestration.rs:241-242 simulate calls 'self.stage_ctx()' and 'self.simulation_ctx()', while train_inner re-inlines StageContext at :147. stage_ctx() does have production consumers (simulation/enumerated.rs:542, training/forward/enumerated.rs:1005), so that constructor is earned and merely bypassed. The doc on training_ctx states its purpose is to let a probe drive production entry points 'without duplicating this crate's private field layout'. crates/cobre-sddp/src/training/backward_pass_state.rs:4811-4812, cited not anchored, records the same bypass in its own words: 'stage_ctx/training_ctx are built as direct field literals (mirroring StudySetup::train_inner), not via the setup.stage_ctx()/...'.
evidence.reading: The constructor exists, the crate's own primary training path does not use it, and the cfg gate is why: production cannot call a cfg(test)-gated method. The result is two hand-synchronised copies of one 19-field context, the accessor copy exercised only by tests. Under the Context Struct Pattern a new datum threaded into training is a new TrainingContext field, which now needs two edits; miss the accessor copy and the tests keep compiling while exercising a context production never builds. The doc on the gated method claims to prevent exactly the duplication that sits 100 lines away in the same module directory.

candidates.fixShape: Un-gate training_ctx to pub(crate), matching stage_ctx, and have train_inner call self.stage_ctx() and self.training_ctx() the way simulate already calls self.stage_ctx() and self.simulation_ctx(), deleting both inlined literals. One constructor then serves production and tests, so a new context field has a single edit site and the gated-mirror drift class disappears. Construction is field-for-field identical, so the change is byte-neutral by inspection; bound it with the parity goldens, the rank-invariance harness, and an mpiexec -n 1 versus -n 2 run because train_inner is the MPI training entry point.

candidates.title: setup/scenario_library_set.rs is a 46-line public module of two impl-less structs whose name collides with the sibling setup/scenario_libraries.rs, which does not contain the type ScenarioLibraries

evidence.command: git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/setup/scenario_library_set.rs ; git grep -n -E '^(pub |pub\(crate\) )?fn ' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/src/setup/scenario_libraries.rs ; git grep -n -E '^(pub |pub\(crate\) )?mod ' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/src/setup/mod.rs ; git grep -n 'ScenarioLibraries|PhaseLibraries' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/src/lib.rs
evidence.output: scenario_library_set.rs is 46 lines end to end: 'pub struct PhaseLibraries' with 7 fields (inflow_scheme, load_scheme, ncs_scheme, historical, external_inflow, external_load, external_ncs) and 'pub struct ScenarioLibraries { pub training: PhaseLibraries, pub simulation: PhaseLibraries }'. Neither type has an impl block of any kind. scenario_libraries.rs holds five functions and no types: build_historical_inflow_library, per_stage_scenario_counts, build_external_inflow_library, build_external_load_library, build_external_ncs_library. setup/mod.rs:59-60 declares 'pub(crate) mod scenario_libraries;' immediately above 'pub mod scenario_library_set;'. The grep for ScenarioLibraries and PhaseLibraries in lib.rs returns nothing, so neither type is re-exported at the crate root and the only path to the aggregate is cobre_sddp::setup::scenario_library_set::ScenarioLibraries. setup/stage_data.rs repeats the shape: 77 lines, one impl-less 'pub struct StageData' with roughly 16 fields and no methods.
evidence.reading: The directive's question resolves as: these are two real structs, not a typedef. The flaw is the module boundary, not the types. Two same-directory modules whose names differ by one noun split the aggregate types from their builders, and the plural-named module is the one without the plural type, so a reader grepping for ScenarioLibraries lands in the file that does not define it. Neither 46-line module carries behaviour that a module boundary buys, and the confusable pair is a standing cost paid on every read of setup/. This is a naming and boundary claim only; it is not the StudySetup field-role claim that CD-005 already owns, and it proposes no change to StudySetup.

candidates.fixShape: Collapse one of the two nouns. Either rename the builder module to scenario_library_builders.rs and let scenario_libraries.rs own the two aggregates, or fold the aggregates into the module that owns their only holder and keep a single scenario_libraries.rs for both types and builders. Fold stage_data.rs the same way if the station wants the pattern settled once rather than twice. The edit is module paths and use lines only, no behaviour and no field moves, and the compiler proves the rename complete, so the parity goldens are a formality rather than the guard.

_needsHuman.question: Does the 'sanctioned #[allow(...)] census' stay excluded-by-construction in the do-not-raise set now that four production sites in the 5a manifest are shown to carry no written rationale?
_needsHuman.context: The prior register excludes the census wholesale on the ground that each site is sanctioned, while attacker-prompt.md's over-engineering lens states that an allow with a written rationale is sanctioned and one without is a candidate. Those two instructions point opposite ways for exactly these four sites, so candidate 1 is raised under OD-009 with reRaiseOf set rather than suppressed. An owner ruling would let later stations apply one rule instead of re-deriving this conflict: either narrow the exclusion to rationale-bearing sites, or keep it whole and route rationale-absent sites somewhere else.
